title: DARE-sparsified task deltas as Mirror codes
hypothesis: After mandatory DARE sparsification, a shared task-delta basis plus compact task codes can reduce actual complete payload bytes while preserving held-out task function quality; gains must exceed native PCA/shared-basis coding and Task Arithmetic/TIES controls.
physical_object: shared base model plus one sparse delta basis across 16 synthetic tasks
mirror_coordinate: per-task coefficients over a shared basis fitted to DARE-sparsified deltas
controls: DARE per-task delta sparsification at identical 90% drop
DARE then PCA basis plus task codes
native PCA/shared-basis coding of DARE deltas

development.selection_metric: held-out function NRMSE against original task deltas, error relative to DARE, complete serialized payload bytes, and merge interference

paid_objects: dense deltas or sparse DARE indices and values

success_gate: At least one DARE+PCA rank across all audit seeds: actual full payload <=75% of DARE payload, original-task function NRMSE no more than DARE NRMSE +.02, and inference arithmetic <=1.25x sparse DARE decode. Mirror-specific value additionally requires strict improvement over canonical native PCA/shared-basis coding at matched bytes; exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: No rank meets the frozen DARE-relative quality/byte/compute gate, or native PCA/shared-basis representation exactly aliases Mirror. Report raw shared-basis, DARE and merge frontiers separately.
boundaries: Synthetic linear task deltas from a shared low-rank basis; no pretrained language model, natural benchmark or actual fine-tuning claim.
The physical basis family is known only to generate tasks; raw-basis results are an oracle-aligned upper bound.
Task Arithmetic and TIES merge one shared delta; their per-task interference metric is not directly equivalent to retaining separate task deltas.
No GPU or production merge runtime conclusion; arithmetic counts are analytic proxies.
